_readme: Wild bee nests per biome. Applied at world load by kubejs/server_scripts/worldgen/bee_nests.js (CEConfig
[worldgen.systems] beeNests) and patcherMod BeeNests. Rejoin the world after editing; only chunks generated
afterwards change. Reference + tests: feature_writeup/bee_nests.md section 3. Per-biome before/after:
Selector: 'where' clauses OR'ed, traits AND'ed, '!x' negated (traits: wild_crops.json biomes); ocean/cave
biomes never match a clause; then 'add' (ids, '#tags') and 'except' (ids).
chance (0-1): every tree in the biome has at least this chance of a nest (trees without one gain it).
scale (0-1000): the trees' own nest chances times this. Per tree: min(1, max(p * scale, chance)).
Rules fold in file order per biome; each sets only the fields it names (later wins).
trees: extra trees carrying nests, { feature, rate ('1/16' = one per 16 chunks), sapling (survival check) }.
Values below are calibrated on measured trees per chunk (bee_nests_baseline.json, scratch server 2026-10-10).

rules._note: Birch and Dark Forest had no nests (Terralith trees); ~14 and ~10 trees/chunk -> about 1 in 25-35 chunks. Forest 1 in 100 -> 1 in 55.
Savannas, shrublands, orchid swamp: none before; savanna ~1 in 160 (sparse acacias). Jungles left out on purpose (no bees in jungles; none before either).
Taigas and cold highland forests, not snowy ones: a rare find, ~1 in 200-250 chunks.
Plains, Sunflower Plains, Meadow, Blooming Plateau: their few trees nest more often.
The bee biomes: their own nest chances doubled (Flower Forest, lavender, sakura, blooming, moonlight).
Showcase bee biomes, about as rich as Sakura / Old Growth Birch: ~1 nest in 10 chunks.
Meadow-type biomes have ~1 tree per 100 chunks: add a lone fancy oak with a nest every ~16 chunks.
Showcase bee biomes with almost no trees of their own: a lone bee oak every ~10 chunks.
